sections.description: Short guide to QuEst: what to set, in which order, and what the simulation returns.

options.title: QuEst — help
options.text:
# QuEst — transient decay of a tethered dye

Predicts the fluorescence decay of a dye on a flexible linker from the
structure alone: the dye diffuses inside its accessible volume, is quenched on
contact with nearby amino acids (PET), and — with FRET enabled — transfers to
an acceptor.

## What to set
1. **Structure** — a PDB/CIF file or a four-character RCSB ID, and the residue
   the dye is attached to.
2. **Dye** — linker length, width and dye radius define the accessible volume.
3. **Simulation** — the unquenched lifetime, the diffusion coefficient and how
   long to simulate. `t_step` must resolve the fastest motion; the defaults are
   measured, not guessed.
4. **Quenching** — per-residue quenching rates and contact radii. Editing a row
   changes the chemistry for that amino acid only.
5. **FRET** — enable it, place the acceptor, and give R₀ **in Ångström**.

## What comes out
Quantum yield and mean lifetime, the donor (and FRET) decay, the dye
trajectory, and its autocorrelation.

Everything in this form is one QuEst *project*. **Save project** writes exactly
the JSON the command line (`quest simulate project.json`) and the web UI read,
so a run started here can be finished anywhere.

sections.title: Project
sections.description: All simulation parameters of the QuEst project, grouped into collapsible panels.

sections.title: Structure
sections.description: Structure file or RCSB ID and the residue to which the dye is attached.

sections.label: Structure file
sections.description: Path to the structure file (PDB/CIF), or a bare four-character RCSB PDB ID used for AV calculation.

sections.label: Attachment chain
sections.description: Chain identifier of the amino acid residue where the dye is tethered.

sections.label: Attachment residue
sections.description: Residue sequence number of the amino acid where the dye is tethered.

sections.label: Attachment atom
sections.description: Atom name (e.g., CB, CA) used as the tethering point for the dye.

sections.title: Dye
sections.description: Linker length, linker width and dye radius that define the dye's accessible volume.

sections.label: Linker length (Å)
sections.description: Maximum distance from attachment point to the center of the dye.

sections.label: Linker width (Å)
sections.description: Width of the linker tethering the dye.

sections.label: Dye radius (Å)
sections.description: Exclusion radius representing the dye sphere (single-sphere approximation).

sections.label: Allowed sphere (Å)
sections.description: Radius around the attachment atom inside which the linker ignores obstacles, so it can leave the atom it is tied to. On by default at FPS's 2.25 Å (0.5 × the 4.5 Å linker width); the attachment atom itself is never an obstacle.

sections.label: Obstacle radius scale
sections.description: Factor on the atoms' van der Waals radii (IMP's united-atom set) when they are obstacles to the linker and the dye. The default, 0.84, matches FPS's smaller Bondi radii: at it the T4L CB-site volumes agree with FPS's own routine. 1.0 uses IMP's radii as they are.

sections.label: Grid resolution (Å)
sections.description: Grid resolution used to compute the accessible volume (AV) and diffusion search space.

sections.title: Simulation
sections.description: Unquenched lifetime, diffusion coefficient and the duration and sampling of the simulation.

sections.label: Unquenched lifetime (ns)
sections.description: Fluorescence lifetime of the donor dye in the absence of quenching.

sections.label: Donor diffusion coefficient (Å²/ns)
sections.description: Diffusion coefficient of the donor dye in solution, when not interacting with the protein surface.

sections.label: Ensemble
sections.description: Where the dye sits during the excited state. 'walk': Brownian walkers, each started from the equilibrium occupancy (w = product of slow_factor^-1 over the residues in range), and a photon race along each; FRET reads the transfer rate off the dyes' trajectories, with Monte-Carlo noise. 'equilibrium': the static limit, every position decays on its own at 1/tau0 + kQ, weighted by w; exact and fast, what the inverse fit uses. 'pde': the diffusion equation on the AV grid with stickiness as a potential and quenching as a sink, solved without sampling noise; it includes motion during the excited state, and its stationary state is the equilibrium ensemble. The walk and the PDE describe the same physics and agree to the walk's time-step bias. Both simulate FRET: the PDE's is the fast-acceptor limit (the acceptor averaged over its volume) entering as a transfer-rate field in the sink, so fret.acceptor_dynamics must be 'averaged'.

sections.label: Simulation time (ns)
sections.description: Simulated time per trajectory block (walk ensemble). The walk covers parallel_trajectories × t_max in all, cut into walkers of 20–50 × tau0 (about 1000 of them) that each start from the equilibrium occupancy. Unused by the equilibrium and PDE ensembles.

sections.label: Time step (ns)
sections.description: Time step of the Brownian walk (walk ensemble). A smaller step shrinks the walk's bias at sticky boundaries; the equilibrium and PDE ensembles do not step.

sections.label: Simulated photons
sections.description: Number of excitation photons simulated to reconstruct the fluorescence decay histogram.

sections.label: Decay bins
sections.description: Number of time channels/bins used to construct the output decay histogram.

sections.label: Coarse-grained structure
sections.description: Reduce the structure to backbone plus CB before simulating, with CB moved to the side-chain centre of mass. Side-chain atoms are then absent, so every residue's quenching centre falls back to that CB pseudo-atom, and the accessible volume grows because side chains no longer block it. This is a modelling choice, not a speed optimisation: QuEst's cost is dominated by the AV grid rather than the atom count.

sections.title: Quenching
sections.description: Quenching distances and rates of the amino acids that quench the dye on contact.

sections.label: Fallback contact radius (Å)
sections.description: Contact radius used by residue types that do not define their own quench_radius. It is measured from the dye centre to the residue's quenching centre, so it must exceed the dye radius plus van der Waals contact (typically 7-9 A for a 3.5 A dye).
Per-residue quenching rate, contact radius, quenching atoms and slow-down factor; editing a row changes only that amino acid.

columns.label: kQ (1/ns)
columns.description: Rate at which this residue type quenches the dye while the two are in contact. Contributions from residues whose contact spheres overlap add up.

columns.label: Radius (Å)
columns.description: Distance from the dye centre to this residue's quenching centre within which quenching occurs. Leave empty to inherit the project-wide critical_distance.

columns.label: Atoms
columns.description: Atom names whose centroid defines this residue's quenching centre. The defaults follow the redox-active moiety that mediates photo-induced electron transfer: the indole ring for TRP, the phenol ring for TYR, the imidazole ring for HIS, SD for MET and SG for CYS - not CB.

columns.label: Slow factor
columns.description: Factor between 0 and 1 scaling the dye's diffusion coefficient near this residue type, modelling unspecific stickiness. Overlapping residues multiply their factors.

sections.title: FRET
sections.description: Enable FRET and define the acceptor position, its dye geometry and the Förster radius R0.

sections.label: FRET enabled
sections.description: Whether a FRET acceptor dye is simulated to compute FRET efficiency and decay curves.

sections.label: Förster radius (Å)
sections.description: Förster radius R0 of the donor–acceptor pair, in Ångström like every other length in a project. Stored as the donor→acceptor cell of fret.R0_matrix; the transfer rate scales as (R0/r)^6, so entering nanometres makes FRET vanish. Typical xanthene pairs are 45–65 Å.

sections.label: Orientation factor κ²
sections.description: Orientation factor κ² of the transfer, between 0 (perpendicular transition dipoles) and 4 (collinear). QuEst does not model it: the dye is a point diffusing in a volume and has no dipole to orient, so this is the averaging regime you are asserting. The default 2/3 is the isotropic dynamic average, which is what a published Förster radius already assumes — leaving it there reproduces the rate exactly. Raise it only with evidence that both dyes are orientationally restricted.

sections.label: Acceptor chain
sections.description: Chain identifier of the residue where the FRET acceptor dye is attached.

sections.label: Acceptor residue
sections.description: Residue sequence number where the FRET acceptor dye is attached.

sections.label: Acceptor atom
sections.description: Atom name where the FRET acceptor dye is attached.

sections.label: Acceptor linker length (Å)
sections.description: Maximum distance from attachment point to the center of the FRET acceptor dye.

sections.label: Acceptor linker width (Å)
sections.description: Width of the linker tethering the FRET acceptor dye.

sections.label: Acceptor dye radius (Å)
sections.description: Exclusion radius representing the FRET acceptor dye sphere.

sections.label: Acceptor diffusion coefficient (Å²/ns)
sections.description: Diffusion coefficient of the FRET acceptor dye when not interacting with the protein surface.

sections.label: Acceptor dynamics
sections.description: How the acceptor is treated: 'trajectory' simulates its Brownian walk with its own diffusion coefficient and stickiness and uses the instantaneous donor-acceptor distance, 'averaged' averages over its static accessible volume (the fast-acceptor limit, valid only when it explores that volume quickly compared with the donor lifetime). The two disagree because a cloud is weighted uniformly while a trajectory is weighted by where the dye dwells. The 'pde' ensemble has no donor trajectory to pair one with, so it requires 'averaged'.

sections.label: Acceptor slowing radius (Å)
sections.description: Radius around each amino-acid centre within which that residue slows the acceptor. Separate from the donor's: a cyanine and a rhodamine do not adhere to a protein surface in the same way. Defaults to the donor's value.

sections.title: Advanced
sections.description: Rarely needed numerical settings such as binning, random seed and parallelism.

sections.label: Parallel trajectories
sections.description: Number of t_max-long trajectory blocks in the walk ensemble. The walkers are vectorised, so this sets the total simulated time, not a thread count. Use -1 for the number of CPU cores, capped at 8.

sections.label: Slowing radius (Å)
sections.description: Radius around each whole-protein amino-acid center where that residue type contributes its slow_factor to the diffusion coefficient grid.

sections.label: Save AV files
sections.description: Whether to save the calculated accessible volume grids as XYZ files.

sections.label: Output file prefix
sections.description: Base filename prefix used when saving simulation outputs, trajectories, and decays.

sections.label: Trajectory skip frames
sections.description: Subsampling factor for writing trajectory frames to coordinates files.

sections.label: Random seed
sections.description: Seed for the Monte-Carlo simulation. When set, both the diffusion trajectory and the photon trace are seeded, so repeated runs of the same project reproduce the same decay and quantum yield exactly. Leave unset for an independent random run; the photon trace then uses a faster multi-threaded kernel.

sections.title: Structure
sections.description: The structure currently loaded as the basis of the simulation.

sections.label: Structure
sections.description: Outcome of the last simulation.

sections.title: Results
sections.description: Simulation status together with the donor decay, dye trajectory and its autocorrelation.

sections.label: State
sections.description: Outcome of the last simulation.

sections.title: Fluorescence decay
sections.description: Donor decay, and the FRET-quenched decay when FRET is enabled.

sections.title: Dye trajectory
sections.description: Distance of the dye from its mean position — how far it actually explores.

sections.title: Position autocorrelation
sections.description: How quickly the dye forgets where it was; sets whether quenching is diffusion- or contact-limited.
